free.note: Cloud Browser free allowance: 15 minutes of browser time across 3 parallel sessions, no card (Google sign-up); no $ credit.

features.ip_note: Residential/mobile/datacenter/ISP IPs in 195+ countries; residential allowance included in cloud plans, overage $1/GB per marketing page vs $1.99/GB proxy traffic in docs; ISP proxies $5/IP.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv 4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Cloud Browser has its own tariff, not the main local antidetect profile subscription. A client OS fingerprint is not a hosted OS SKU.

Official sources conflict: the current Cloud Browser landing offer is $4.50/$8/$14 with 50/100/200 hours, 1/2/3 sessions and $1/GB; the Cloud Browser docs still say $0.048/hour, 20–200 hours, 1–4 sessions and $1.99/GB; general subscription docs publish a different $9/$119/$299 monthly ladder with 100/200/300 cloud hours. Favor the product landing offer but obtain a binding account quote.
Additional concurrency is an add-on, not a requirement to buy 50 separate subscriptions. Engine base plans conservatively retain included concurrency rather than assuming arbitrary add-on approval.
No cap on active Cloud Browser session time (official examples: a nine-hour run stays one session).

fleet.verification: Google signup, free key without card.
fleet.tiers: Intro API key: 3 parallel sessions / 15 total minutes; paid plans have 1–4 included slots; additional concurrency/custom packages by contact.
fleet.notes: Current cloud-browser FAQ establishes 3 for the new free key, unlike old card entry paid 1. Published paid included slots are not a cap if add-ons purchased; large fleet max/approval timing not established.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Every time you run and close a Gologin profile, the system automatically creates a **session snapshot**.
snapshot_auto.note: Browser-profile state only: cookies, session storage, logged-in state, website tokens and browser data. No memory or running processes. It is triggered on profile close, and profile sync uploads the state to the cloud and restores it on the next launch. The last 5 sessions can be restored from Profile > History in the app, and no API for this was found in the OpenAPI spec. The page is written for profiles in general (desktop app), but Cloud Browser runs the same profiles ('Gologin profiles persist. Log in once, close the session, reconnect later'). Not verified live on a cloud session.

harness_api.quote: AI agents typically do not "connect to a browser" directly. Instead, they:
harness_api.note: Cloud Browser is a remote Orbita/Chromium runtime reached over CDP. The agent (Claude, Codex...) runs on the customer's side. First-party MCP server, Claude Code skills and Agent Browser / Web Access CLIs let an outside agent drive the browser, but nothing runs an agent harness inside the environment.
